subject: Interim: Token queue backpressure affecting hosted inference (follow-up & next steps)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@quantiq.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interim: Token queue backpressure affecting hosted inference (initial notice)

Hi Amelia —

I wanted to reach out directly to let you know we're seeing elevated token queueing on our hosted inference fleet that is intermittently increasing tail latency for streaming generation calls (p95 -> p99). Early telemetry shows the impact concentrated on requests that use long-context prompts with high concurrency from a small subset of customers — QuantIQ appears in that signal and we are actively investigating.

What we know so far:
- Start time: ~2027-04-25 08:45 PDT
- Symptom: increased p99 token latencies and request queue growth leading to transient 5xxs for some streaming sessions
- Scope: partial impact for hosted API in us-west region; not all requests affected

Immediate mitigation in progress:
- We’ve throttled background prefetch and disabled a non-critical prefix-caching experiment to free capacity.
- Autoscaler rules adjusted to prioritize latency SLOs for active customers.

Next steps (short):
- We will provide an update in 60–90 minutes with metrics and a tentative remediation time.
- If you see errors from your side (client-side cancelations, 5xxs, or stream truncation), please forward logs and request ids to devops@quantiq.ai and paste the most recent request_id here.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is disruptive to your workflows. I’ll stay on this and loop in our infra lead (Marissa) for a technical update.

—Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:02:30-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim: Token queue backpressure affecting hosted inference (initial notice)

Connor —

Heads-up on what we’re seeing in the infra bridge: a steady increase in KV cache eviction time during heavy prefix loads which creates backpressure on the tokenization stage; that in turn delays KV cache population and extends in-flight token processing windows. Turning off the experimental prefix-caching reduces population churn immediately, but we need to follow with a hotfix to address a race in the cache pump that amplifies latency under concurrent prefix writes.

Short plan:
- 10:15 PDT: roll a conservative hotfix to the cache pump (read-only guard for parallel prep) — quick rollout and roll-backable.
- 10:30 PDT: validate p95/p99 drop and monitor 2x the typical traffic window.
- If metrics improve, we’ll re-enable a refined caching path behind a limited experiment gate.

Ben — please prepare an incident bulletin for the status page with the minimal impact description and link to the postmortem doc stub.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:01:45-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim: Token queue backpressure affecting hosted inference (initial notice)

Hi Amelia — quick update: we deployed the hotfix at 10:15 PDT and immediately observed queue depth decrease and p99 token latency trending back toward baseline. We’re continuing to monitor.

Impact summary for your ops team:
- Observed client errors: intermittent stream resets and 5xxs between 08:45–10:15 PDT for a subset of long-context streaming calls.
- Action taken: experimental prefix-caching disabled; cache pump hotfix deployed; autoscaler bias adjusted.
- Recommended temporary mitigations for QuantIQ (optional): throttle high-concurrency sampling (reduce concurrency per session by ~25%) if you need immediate client-side relief.

We have attached a sample queue snapshot and ingestion logs that show queue depth and token processing latency by shard. I’ll post a concise status page entry in the next 20 minutes and follow up with a full RCA within 48 hours.

Thanks for the logs — the request ids you shared matched error patterns we saw (rq_3d9f). If anything new appears, please send new request ids and we’ll correlate.

—Connor

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@quantiq.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T17:38:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Post-incident update & postmortem link (QuantIQ impact)

Amelia —

Thanks for working through this with us today. Per our commitment, here is the summary and next steps:

Summary of incident:
- Root cause (preliminary): a race condition in the prefix-caching pump under concurrent writes that caused KV eviction delays and tokenization stalls, producing transient queue growth and increased p99 token latency for long-context streaming calls in us-west.
- Impact window: 2027-04-25 08:45–10:20 PDT.
- Customer impact: intermittent stream resets and several 5xx errors for long-context sessions; QuantIQ saw retries and client errors in that window.

Actions completed:
- Disabled experimental prefix-caching (immediate reduction in population churn).
- Rolled hotfix to the cache pump to guard against parallel prep races (10:15 PDT).
- Adjusted autoscaler policy to favor latency SLOs during the recovery window.

What we’ll do next:
- Complete a full RCA and timeline; deliver a written postmortem within 48 hours.
- Provide a mitigations playbook we recommend for long-context customers (client-side concurrency knobs, model/sequence hints).
- Schedule a 30-minute technical review with your SREs next week to walk through the hotfix and long-term fixes.

Postmortem draft (private): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qX-postmortem-20270425
Incident status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-04-25-token-queue

If you’d like us to open a temporary support alias for QuantIQ for the next 72 hours so we can triage any follow-on errors faster, we’re happy to.

Best —
